title: All sufficiently large ample powers embed over an affine base
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample on $T$ in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there is an integer $d_0\geq1$ such that for every integer $d\geq d_0$ there are an integer $r_d\geq0$ and an immersion $j_d:T\to\mathbf P^{r_d}_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $j_d^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L^{\otimes d}$. Here the projective space is [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], its degree-one twist is [def-pc-projective-space-twist], tensor powers are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $j_d^*$ is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. The same statement includes $T=\varnothing$ and the zero ring $A$.

source.place: Tag 01VS (lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S), first paragraph for one power and final paragraph for every sufficiently large power, specialized to an affine base; global generation is Properties Tag 01Q3 (proposition-characterize-ample) and the Segre embedding is Constructions Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding).

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] to choose $a\geq1$, $m\geq0$ and an immersion $j:T\to\mathbf P^m_S$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, over $S$, with $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L^{\otimes a}$. This supplies only one exponent; retain this fixed $a$ throughout.

source.place: Tag 01VS, lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S, first proof paragraph and start of final paragraph

proof.text: The structure module $\mathcal O_T$ is finite type and quasi-coherent: on every affine chart it is the module associated to the ring, generated by $1$ [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_T$. Choose an integer $b\geq1$ such that every $L^{\otimes e}$, $e\geq b$, has finitely many generating global sections. The tensor unit identifies $\mathcal O_T\otimes L^{\otimes e}$ with $L^{\otimes e}$. Put $d_0=a+b\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 01VS, final paragraph, the choice of d_1 using Properties Tag 01Q3 (proposition-characterize-ample), (1) implies (7)

proof.text: Fix $d\geq d_0$ and put $e=d-a\geq b$. Choose generators $t_1,\ldots,t_q$ of $L^{\otimes e}$, adding a zero section if necessary so $q\geq1$. In each rank-one stalk a generating family contains a unit coefficient (otherwise its coefficients all lie in the maximal ideal), hence the nonvanishing loci of the $t_i$ cover $T$. Tensor powers are invertible by induction using [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-sections-morphism-to-proj-polynomial-ring] gives $j_e:T\to\mathbf P^{q-1}_S$ over $S$ with $j_e^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L^{\otimes e}$. The relative projective space over affine $S$ is precisely this polynomial Proj, by its defining affine restriction [def-nagata-relative-projective-space].

source.place: Tag 01VS, final paragraph, sections s-double-prime and their morphism j-prime

proof.text: By [lem-chow-tuple-immersion], $h=(j,j_e):T\to P=\mathbf P^m_S\times_S\mathbf P^{q-1}_S$ is an immersion. The Segre map $\sigma:P\to\mathbf P^{(m+1)q-1}_S$ is a closed immersion by [lem-chow-segre]. Set $j_d=\sigma h$. To verify it is an immersion directly, factor $h$ as a closed immersion into an open $U\subset P$. Since $\sigma$ identifies $P$ with a closed subscheme, choose an open $V$ of the target with $\sigma^{-1}V=U$. Then $U\to V$ is a closed immersion by base change [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; its composite with $T\to U$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products]. Following by $V$ into the target is the required closed-open factorization. All maps are over $S$, and $(m+1)q-1\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 01VS, final paragraph: factorization through the product and the Segre embedding

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-segre-hyperplane-pullback] and the tensor and composite pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor] to obtain $$j_d^*\mathcal O(1)\cong h^*(p_1^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes p_2^*\mathcal O(1))\cong j^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes j_e^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L^{\otimes a}\otimes L^{\otimes e}\cong L^{\otimes d}.$$ The last isomorphism regroups $a+e=d$ tensor factors using associativity [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This proves every required exponent. No step assumes $T$ nonempty: padding the generating family allows $q=1$ for empty $T$. If $A=0$, a map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A=\varnothing$ forces $T=\varnothing$, so this case is included too.

source.place: Tag 01VS, final paragraph: the pullback module of the product-section morphism; Constructions Tag 01WD, lemma-segre-embedding

proof_origin.place: Tag 01VS, lemma-quasi-projective-finite-type-over-S, final paragraph after the one-power construction; using Properties 01Q3 and Constructions 01WD. The closed-open factorization spells out the permanence of immersion used there.

lean.note: Uses the recorded relative-Proj scheme and structure map. Its affine-top restrictionIso, preceded by topIso.inv, transports the existing Proj.twist in degree one to that scheme.
